items.title: Add Smart Item Batching with Conflict Detection for Autopilot
items.prd_content:
# PRD: Add Smart Item Batching with Conflict Detection for Autopilot

## Problem Statement

### Current Situation
Autopilot executes items one at a time without awareness of potential code conflicts. When multiple approved items touch the same files or components, sequential execution can cause merge conflicts, test failures, or overwrites.

### Root Cause Analysis
The existing DependencyAnalysis system provides rich file-level data but execution engine does not leverage it for intelligent batching.

### Impact Assessment
- **Primary Users Affected**: Power users automating large improvements, automation/DevOps teams
- **Problem Frequency**: On every multi-item execution cycle (daily-weekly)
- **Current Workaround**: Manual sequential execution with careful file monitoring spreadsheets
- **Business Cost**: Reduced confidence in system reliability, support escalations, process bottlenecks

## Proposed Solution

### Solution Overview
Implement intelligent item batching that analyzes target_files and affected_files from the existing DependencyAnalysis data to detect potential conflicts. Group non-conflicting items for parallel execution and flag conflicting items for sequential handling.

### Architecture & Integration

- **ConflictDetectionService**: Analyzes DependencyAnalysis records, builds dependency graph
- **BatchingPlanner**: Groups items into parallel-safe batches using graph coloring
- **Modified ExecutionController**: Manages batch-level execution with coordination
- **Monitoring Dashboard**: Shows batch composition and conflict analysis
- **Integration Point**: ExecutionController.execute() → analyzeAndBatch() → executeBatches()


## Success Criteria

- [ ] **Functional**: Conflict detection correctly identifies file overlaps with <5% false positive rate
- [ ] **Performance**: Execution time reduced by 40%+ for non-conflicting items
- [ ] **User Satisfaction**: 85%+ of users report improved confidence

## Technical Approach

### Wave 1: Exploration (1-2 weeks)

| Task | Owner | Duration | Deliverable |
|------|-------|----------|-------------|
| Analyze DependencyAnalysis schema and build graph models | Architecture | 3 days | Design doc + pseudocode |
| Design conflict detection algorithm (graph theory) | Design | 3 days | Algorithm doc + visual mockups |
| Create conflict test scenarios | QA | 2 days | 15+ test scenarios |
| API/schema impact audit | Backend | 1 day | Breaking change assessment |

### Wave 2: Implementation (2-3 weeks)

| Task | Owner | Duration | Testing |
|------|-------|----------|---------|
| Core service implementation | Backend | 4 days | Unit tests (95%+ coverage) |
| Integration with existing systems | Backend/Frontend | 3 days | Integration tests |
| UI/UX implementation | Frontend | 2 days | Visual regression tests |
| Docs, training, deployment | Docs/DevOps | 1 day | Updated guides, runbooks |

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-------------|--------|-----------|
| Conflict detection false positives reduce parallelization benefit | Medium | High | Conservative algorithm; tunable sensitivity; monitor actual false positive rate |
| Race conditions in parallel execution | Medium | Critical | Distributed locks per-file; atomic transactions; comprehensive logging |
| Performance degradation at scale | Low | High | Batch size limits; caching strategy; profile against 1000+ items |
| User confusion about new patterns | Medium | Medium | UX testing with 5+ users; inline help; documentation |

## Out of Scope

- Custom conflict resolution strategies, CI/CD integration beyond git, interactive conflict UI
- Third-party integrations (defer to plugin system)
- Extensive performance optimization (baseline acceptable)

## Key Metrics & Success Tracking

- **Adoption**: 60%+ of multi-item executions use batching
- **Quality**: <5% false positive rate
- **User Impact**: {{isAutopilot ? "40%+ faster execution times" : "50%+ reduction in related support tickets"}}

# PRD: Add Execution History with Diff Preview and Rollback Capability

## Problem Statement

### Current Situation
Once items are marked completed, users have no way to see what code changes were made or revert problematic implementations.

### Root Cause Analysis
Execution progress data exists but is ephemeral - once marked complete, no audit trail remains.

### Impact Assessment
- **Primary Users Affected**: Users concerned about changeability, compliance officers, code reviewers
- **Problem Frequency**: Post-execution review (2-3 times per week)
- **Current Workaround**: Git log inspection + manual PR history searching
- **Business Cost**: Reduced confidence in system reliability, support escalations, process bottlenecks

## Proposed Solution

### Solution Overview
Extend the execution_progress table to capture git commit SHAs and diffs for each completed item. Add a 'Changes' tab showing actual code diff. Implement rollback action that creates revert PR.

### Architecture & Integration

- **ExecutionHistoryStore**: Captures git commit SHA and diffs post-execution
- **DiffPreviewModal**: Displays file-level changes with syntax highlighting
- **RollbackService**: Creates revert PRs with safety checks
- **Enhanced ExecutionProgressRecord**: Adds git_commit_sha, diff_stats fields
- **Integration Point**: completeExecution() → captureGitMetadata() → persistExecutionHistory()


## Success Criteria

- [ ] **Functional**: All completed executions preserve full git history and enable 1-click rollback
- [ ] **Performance**: No measurable impact on dashboard performance
- [ ] **User Satisfaction**: 85%+ of users report improved confidence

# PRD: Add Configurable Webhook Notifications for Execution Events

## Problem Statement

### Current Situation
Users can only see execution status through the dashboard in real-time. There is no way to receive notifications when autopilot completes runs or executions fail when away from the dashboard.

### Root Cause Analysis
Dashboard-only visibility creates blind spots for users who need out-of-band notifications.

### Impact Assessment
- **Primary Users Affected**: Users who need 24/7 execution awareness, remote teams
- **Problem Frequency**: Whenever long-running execution completes (multiple times daily)
- **Current Workaround**: Constant dashboard polling or manual completion checks
- **Business Cost**: Reduced confidence in system reliability, support escalations, process bottlenecks

## Proposed Solution

### Solution Overview
Add webhook configuration in Settings allowing users to specify endpoints for execution events. Implement server-side webhook dispatch. Support Slack, Discord, email via webhook templates.

### Architecture & Integration

- **WebhookManager**: Handles user webhook configuration and validation
- **EventDispatcher**: Fires execution lifecycle events (started, completed, failed)
- **RetryQueue**: Handles delivery failures with exponential backoff
- **WebhookTemplate System**: Pre-built Slack, Discord, email formatters
- **Integration Point**: ExecutionController state transitions → dispatch(event) → deliver via webhooks


## Success Criteria

- [ ] **Functional**: Webhooks deliver with 99.5% success rate and <30 second latency
- [ ] **Performance**: No measurable impact on dashboard performance
- [ ] **User Satisfaction**: 80%+ reduction in clarification questions

# PRD: Add success microinteractions for inline approve/reject actions
